findings.evidence: Before writing, confirm every citation resolves: the file and line exist, the issue number exists, the metric or query name is real.
findings.fix: Shorten this to one clause, 'Drop or relabel as hypothesis any citation you did not open in this session'. The model already knows to check that citations exist. Keep only the rule it would miss: an unverified citation becomes a hypothesis and is never deleted without saying so.

findings.evidence: Rank within each tier; five to ten ideas in total by default
findings.fix: Add one ranking rule inside a tier. For example: 'within a tier, order by reach x evidence strength / (effort + adoption cost); break ties toward the idea with the cheapest test'. Right now the model invents its own weighting, and two runs on the same evidence can rank ideas differently.

findings.evidence: | Rank | Idea | Priority | Evidence or hypothesis | Value mechanism | Reach (...) | Adoption cost (...) | Effort (...) | Risk (...) | Deciding trade-off | Assumption to validate |
findings.fix: Keep the rule that every field must be present. Allow one escape hatch: when cells would run past about 20 words, render each idea as a short block with labeled lines (Mechanism, Reach, Effort, ...). An 11-column table is rigid for ideation output and hard to read in long sessions.

Make the file paths relative to the skill root, as evaluating-skills.md does ("evals/files/habit-repo/README.md", ...). Also add an eval where the prompt gives no user count, with the assertion 'Reach cells use the unknown-share form and name the metric to measure'. That branch is currently untested.

findings.evidence: Every Reach cell names the user-base number from the request or evidence, in the template's form.
findings.fix: Add a fallback for the no-number branch, for example the trigger query 'help us decide what product opportunity to pursue next': 'When neither request nor evidence gives a user base, write "unknown share of unknown base; measure <active users of the affected flow>" and add that count as a validation question.'

findings.evidence: write a short comparison instead of the full session tables
findings.fix: Say whether the single-feature comparison is still saved as session-N.md through step 5, and which template sections it keeps. For example: 'Still save it as the next session-N.md, with Scope, Baseline, the comparison table and Validation questions.' Also state that session 1 omits the 'Previous:' line.
